Working in /opt/nxeon-v2 (Next.js app, branch design/v2, a hosting platform). This is a WRITE task — make real code changes, going to production soon.

**IMPORTANT CONSTRAINT — read before touching anything:** `components/nx/RackHero.tsx` and `components/nx/Ribbons.tsx` (the dashboard's aurora ribbon-stream background) were explicitly reverted to their original state after repeated "fixes" made them worse, per direct owner instruction. Do NOT touch these two files under any circumstances, even if they seem related to what you're fixing.

**Fix 1 — Verify-email and impersonation banners are unreadable in light mode.**
`components/nx/Banners.tsx` (`VerifyEmailBanner`, `ImpersonationBanner`, sharing a `Banner` wrapper around lines 32-160) paints a hardcoded dark-navy background (`rgba(1,15,34,0.86)` and `rgba(1,15,34,0.88)`, roughly lines 48 and 134) that never changes with the theme, while its text uses theme-aware tokens (`text-white`/`text-tx-body`) that flip to near-black ink in light mode — producing near-invisible dark-on-dark text for a real customer with an unverified email, in light mode. Fix by making the banner's own background theme-aware too, matching how OTHER fixed-position elements in this same file (or `app/globals.css`) already correctly handle a similar "always readable in both themes" requirement — check if there's an existing `.nx-dark-island` class pattern being used elsewhere for intentionally-always-dark surfaces (if so, and if the intent is for these banners to ALSO always stay dark regardless of theme, apply that class consistently and ALSO fix the text color to not flip in that case) OR make both background and text properly theme-token-driven so they track together correctly in both themes (check `app/globals.css` for the relevant `--color-*` tokens already used elsewhere for banner-like surfaces, e.g. cards). Pick whichever approach matches the codebase's own established convention — read `app/globals.css`'s comments around `.nx-dark-island` and any existing banner/card light-mode overrides to decide correctly, don't guess. Verify by reading how `NotificationsPanel` (also in this file, unaffected per a prior audit because it's inside `.nx-dark-island` header scope) already gets this right, and apply the same fix to `VerifyEmailBanner`/`ImpersonationBanner`.

**Fix 2 — Claude Code/Build defaults to enabled, unlike Sites and Calendar.**
`lib/settings.ts` has `feature_claude_builder: "true"` in `SETTINGS_DEFAULTS` (around line 430), while `feature_website_builder` and `feature_calendar` are NOT in `SETTINGS_DEFAULTS` at all (so they resolve to `false` via an explicit fallback at their one call site in `app/dashboard/layout.tsx`, lines ~137-138). Change `feature_claude_builder`'s default in `SETTINGS_DEFAULTS` to `"false"`, so it's consistent with the other two dormant features and doesn't expose a real AI-builder-with-SSH-execution feature to every new customer by default. The feature itself is fully real and functional — this is purely a default-off-until-explicitly-enabled change, not disabling the code.

**Fix 3 — Sites and Calendar are nav-hidden only, not route-gated.**
`app/dashboard/sites/page.tsx` and `app/dashboard/calendar/page.tsx` currently only call `requireUser()` — a customer who bookmarks or guesses the URL bypasses the hidden nav item entirely and gets the full feature regardless of the `feature_website_builder`/`feature_calendar` settings. Add a route-level check to BOTH pages matching the pattern already used correctly in `lib/actions-claude.ts`'s `submitBuild` and `lib/actions-claude-console.ts`'s `planConsoleBuild` (both call `getSettingBool("feature_claude_builder", true)` — or now `false` after fix 2 — and refuse when off) — but since these are PAGE components not actions, the right pattern is: check the flag near the top of the page's server component (after `requireUser()`), and if off, either `notFound()` or redirect to `/dashboard` (check how other flag-gated pages in this codebase, if any, handle this — search for `getSettingBool` usage inside `app/dashboard/**/page.tsx` files for a precedent; if none exists, use Next.js's `notFound()` from `next/navigation`, which is already used elsewhere in this codebase for similar "not available" cases).

After each fix, run `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && npx tsc --noEmit` and resolve any type errors. Do not touch files outside `components/nx/Banners.tsx`, `app/globals.css`, `lib/settings.ts`, `app/dashboard/sites/page.tsx`, `app/dashboard/calendar/page.tsx`. Do not commit — leave changes unstaged. Report back file-by-file with line numbers and what you changed.

content.content: # Nxeon v2 — the "Nexion" design fork **This is not the production tree.** It is a full fork of the Nxeon platform with a from-scratch visual language called **Nexion** built over the real backend. The code is real, the database is real, the money paths are real code — but `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, so no VM is ever provisioned and no card is ever charged. Read `docs/NEXION-V2.md` next. This file is the operating manual; that one is the direction and the history of what has been built. --- ## Where you are, and what that changes This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's commits. The script checks for this and stops; take the stop seriously. ## The tree | | | |---|---| | Path | `/opt/nxeon-v2` | | Branch | `design/v2` | | Service | `nxeon-v2-web` on port **3021** | | Public URL | https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud | | Database | `nxeon_v2` on localhost — **separate** from prod and from the primary's own copy | | Logins | `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt` (admin + a design customer account) | | Build log | `/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log` | `rebuild.sh` skips the marketing site by default (~137 of ~195 route files, and it dominates a build we run by hand after every change). `NX_FULL=1 ./rebuild.sh` builds everything — do that before any staging or prod pass. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. Use `scripts/node1.sh` rather than raw ssh — quoting a psql call through two levels of ssh is where this reliably goes wrong: ```bash scripts/node1.sh cards "dashboard" # find concept cards by title scripts/node1.sh board # list that card's attachments scripts/node1.sh pull # copy them to /tmp/board/ scripts/node1.sh db "select …" # query against PROD scripts/node1.sh sh '' # anything else ``` **That grant is wide, and node-1 runs every customer VM, the production database and the mail server — mistakes here are not sandboxed.** The `db` subcommand refusing obvious writes is a guard against a slip, not a security boundary; the access itself is full root. **Update, 2026-09-12: the owner authorized this session to build, deploy, and promote the Nexion portal to production directly from here** — including running `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` and `scripts/promote-production.sh` on node-1, and writing to the prod DB as those scripts require (`prisma db push --accept-data-loss` on the way to production is the expected, sanctioned behavior of that script, not a mistake to avoid). This supersedes the "treat it as read-only, ask first" rule that used to sit here — the routine build/deploy/promote path no longer needs a stop-and-ask. That authorization carries guardrails that are **not optional**: - **Take a fresh, named `pg_dump` snapshot immediately before any write to the prod DB**, the same discipline already used for the pre-merge backup (`pre--.dump` under `/root/db-backups` on node-1, pulled down to node-2 too). Never skip this because a daily timer already ran — the daily timer isn't synced to the moment you're about to change something. - **Stop and report before proceeding if a step turns out more destructive or irreversible than expected** — e.g. `prisma db push --accept-data-loss` reporting it would actually drop a column or table rather than just add one, a schema change that isn't purely additive, or anything that would disrupt a customer mid-session in a way the sanctioned scripts don't already account for. "Automatic" covers the routine, expected path; it does not mean an unexpected destructive step gets waved through. - **Anything outside the build/deploy/promote workflow is still stop-and-ask** — touching customer credentials, hand-editing `/opt/nxeon` outside the sanctioned scripts, restarting a service those scripts don't themselves restart, or touching any of the `/opt/nxeon-*` siblings that belong to other sessions. The authorization is for shipping this fork to production, not a blanket lift of every caution on this box. ## Rules that are not negotiable 1. **Never fabricate.** No invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, ETAs or capabilities. If a number cannot be read from the database or from a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why. This tree has already had hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not reintroduce that shape. - Root cause confirmed: this is a Tailwind v4 `@theme` setup where `text-white`/`text-tx-body`/`text-tx-mute` all resolve through `--color-*` CSS custom properties, and `html[data-theme="light"]` re-declares those tokens to dark-ink values for readability elsewhere in the app. The banners' backgrounds are hardcoded dark navy in both themes (correct, since these must always be legible dark alert bars), but their text was still riding the theme-flipping tokens — hence dark-on-dark. `.nx-dark-island` (defined in `app/globals.css` lines 462–537, and used the same way by `NotificationsPanel`'s ancestor `header.nx-dark-island` in `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) re-pins those same tokens back to their dark-theme values inside the subtree, in light mode. Since it's a no-op in dark mode (verified: every `.nx-dark-island` rule in `globals.css` is scoped under `html[data-theme="light"]`), this is a purely additive fix with no dark-mode regression risk.
